series.title: Integration, assessment and remediation
covers: Different expressions of greetings
Different expressions of leave taking
Introducing one's family members, friends…, responding to introductions and asking for and giving personal information
Getting someone to clarify or repeat something they had said

items.title: Formal / informal
items.text: Rewrite in a formal way: «Hi! What's up?»
items.solution: Good morning/afternoon. How are you?

items.title: Right greeting
items.text:
What do you say?
a) You meet your teacher at 9 a.m.  b) You meet a friend.  c) You meet a visitor for the first time.
items.solution: a) Good morning, sir/madam.  b) Hi! How are you?  c) How do you do? / Nice to meet you.

items.title: Family members
items.text: Complete: My uncle's son is my ___. My sister's daughter is my ___. My father's father is my ___.
items.solution: cousin – niece – grandfather

items.title: Spell
items.text: What do you say when you don't know how to write a name?
items.solution: How do you spell it, please?

items.title: Complete
items.text: Complete: «It was nice ___ you.» – «See you ___ next week.» – «Give my regards ___ your parents.»
items.solution: meeting/seeing – (no word) / next week ; to

items.title: Speak slowly
items.text: Your teacher speaks fast. What do you say politely?
items.solution: Could you speak more slowly, please?

items.title: Reply
items.text: Reply to: «Long time no see!» – «How is your family?»
items.solution: Yes, it's been a long time! – They are fine, thank you.

items.title: Reading
items.text:
Read: «I'm Aïcha. This is my brother Mohamed. He is 16 and he is a student at the lycée. He wants to be a doctor.»
a) How old is Mohamed? b) What does he want to be?
items.solution: a) He is 16. b) He wants to be a doctor.

items.title: Dialogue
items.text:
Complete:
A: Good afternoon, Mr. Ba. How are you?
B: ___ , thank you. And ___?
A: Very well, ___.
items.solution: Fine/I'm fine ; you ; thanks

items.title: Respond
items.text: How do you respond when someone says: «This is my brother, Ali.»?
items.solution: Nice to meet you, Ali. / Pleased to meet you.

items.title: Personal questions
items.text: Write questions for: a) His name is Omar. b) He lives in Nouadhibou. c) His phone number is 22 00 00 00.
items.solution: a) What is his name? b) Where does he live? c) What is his phone number?

items.title: Write
items.text: Write a short dialogue (4 lines) where two friends say goodbye.
items.solution: A: I must go now. B: OK, see you tomorrow. A: Bye, take care! B: You too!

items.title: Dialogue order
items.text: Put in order: a) Bye! Take care. b) I have to go now. c) OK. See you later. d) Already? It's early.
items.solution: b – d – c – a

items.title: Situations
items.text:
What do you say?
a) You leave your friend after school.  b) You go to bed.  c) Your friend is travelling.
items.solution: a) See you tomorrow!  b) Good night!  c) Have a nice trip!

items.title: Meaning
items.text: Ask about the meaning of the word «brave».
items.solution: What does «brave» mean?

items.title: Introduce
items.text: Introduce your friend Khadi (13, from Rosso, likes reading) to your teacher.
items.solution: Sir, this is my friend Khadi. She is 13. She is from Rosso. She likes reading.

items.title: Clarify
items.text: Write three ways to ask someone to repeat.
items.solution: Pardon? – Can you repeat, please? – Could you say that again, please? – Sorry, I didn't understand.

items.title: Leave taking
items.text: Write four expressions used to say goodbye.
items.solution: Goodbye. – See you soon. – Take care. – Have a nice day. – Good night.

items.title: Dialogue
items.text:
Complete:
A: My name is Yacoub.
B: Sorry, ___ ?
A: Yacoub. Y-A-C-O-U-B.
B: Thank you.
items.solution: Could you repeat, please? / How do you spell it?

items.title: Greeting card
items.text: Write a short Eid greeting message to a friend.
items.solution: Eid Mubarak, dear …! I wish you and your family a happy Eid. Best wishes.

series.title: Integration, assessment and remediation
covers: Talking about one's family members, friends, town, home…, and say where they are located
Talking and asking about religious, social and professional obligations
Comparing people and things using short and long adjectives
Counting (50-1000)
Expressing and asking about quantity using quantifiers (many, much, a lot of, few, a few, little, a little…)
Making and responding to orders
Making and responding to requests

items.title: Numbers
items.text: Write in letters: 65 – 100 – 248 – 999.
items.solution: sixty-five – one hundred – two hundred and forty-eight – nine hundred and ninety-nine

items.title: Requests
items.text: Make polite requests: (open the window) (lend me your pen)
items.solution: Could you open the window, please? – Can you lend me your pen, please?

items.title: Correct
items.text: Correct: «My brother is more tall than me.» «This exercise is easyer.»
items.solution: My brother is taller than me. This exercise is easier.

items.title: Orders
items.text: Make polite orders: (a glass of water) (the bill)
items.solution: Can I have a glass of water, please? – The bill, please.

items.title: At the restaurant
items.text:
Complete:
Waiter: What would you ___?
Customer: I'd ___ rice with fish, please.
Waiter: Anything to ___?
items.solution: like – like – drink

items.title: Comparatives
items.text: Write the comparative: tall – big – happy – beautiful – good.
items.solution: taller – bigger – happier – more beautiful – better

items.title: Questions
items.text: Make questions: (you – have to – wear a uniform)
items.solution: Do you have to wear a uniform?

items.title: Much / many
items.text: Complete with much / many: How ___ books? How ___ water? There aren't ___ people.
items.solution: many – much – many

items.title: Some / any
items.text: Complete: There is ___ bread. Are there ___ eggs? There isn't ___ rice.
items.solution: some – any – any

items.title: Figures
items.text: Write in figures: three hundred and twelve – seven hundred and five.

items.title: Must / have to
items.text: Complete with must / mustn't: Muslims ___ pray five times a day. Pupils ___ cheat in exams.
items.solution: must – mustn't

items.title: Responding
items.text: Respond positively and negatively: «Can you help me?»
items.solution: Yes, of course. / Sure. — Sorry, I can't. I'm busy.

items.title: There is / there are
items.text: Complete: In my house ___ three rooms. ___ a big kitchen. ___ any garden? No, ___ .
items.solution: there are – There is – Is there – there isn't

items.title: Compare
items.text: Compare: Nouakchott / Atar (big). A car / a bike (expensive).
items.solution: Nouakchott is bigger than Atar. A car is more expensive than a bike.

items.title: My town
items.text: Write 5 sentences about your town (name, location, places, people).
items.solution: My town is Kiffa. It is in the south of Mauritania. There is a big market and a hospital. People are friendly.

items.title: Location
items.text: Answer: Where is Nouakchott? (on the Atlantic coast)
items.solution: It is on the Atlantic coast.

items.title: Few / little
items.text: Complete with a few / a little: I have ___ friends. There is ___ milk.
items.solution: a few – a little

items.title: Prices
items.text: A bag costs 450 MRU. Write the price in letters.
items.solution: four hundred and fifty ouguiyas

items.title: Responding
items.text: How does a waiter respond to an order?
items.solution: Certainly. / Here you are. / Right away.

items.title: Questions
items.text: Ask about quantity: (sugar) (apples)
items.solution: How much sugar is there? – How many apples are there?

Exercise 1 : Few / little
Complete with a few / a little: I have ___ friends. There is ___ milk.

Exercise 2 : Orders
Make polite orders: (a glass of water) (the bill)

Exercise 3 : Requests
Make polite requests: (open the window) (lend me your pen)
items.solution:
Exercise 1
a few – a little

Exercise 2
Can I have a glass of water, please? – The bill, please.

Exercise 3
Could you open the window, please? – Can you lend me your pen, please?

items.title: Proposal 18 — Term 3 exam
items.text:
Exercise 1 : Questions
Ask about quantity: (sugar) (apples)

Exercise 2 : Some / any
Complete: There is ___ bread. Are there ___ eggs? There isn't ___ rice.

Exercise 3 : Responding
Respond positively and negatively: «Can you help me?»
items.solution:
Exercise 1
How much sugar is there? – How many apples are there?

Exercise 2
some – any – any

Exercise 3
Yes, of course. / Sure. — Sorry, I can't. I'm busy.
